models.apiDescription: The XR3 is to escorts what GTi was for Golfs. It was *the* model to have. Altho the great looks, the pre facelift XR3 featured ford's CHT 1.6 inline-4 and... well, it was anemic, to put it lightly. Both GM's and VW's enterings in the South American hothatch market, the VW Gol GTi and Chevrolet Astra GSi completely dominated the poor XR3. However, due to a partnership with VW of all things, the XR3i released the next year, featuring the facelifted parts and a 1.8 SPFI VW engine. However, even still, it wasn't faster than the competition. The facelifted XR3 remains one of the few affordable hothatches in 2022. This model is based on the South American XR3. It is low-poly, game ready and features fully skinnable, UV-Mapped body.

models.apiDescription:
The 2010 Nissan Versa 1.8 SL is a compact car (often offered as a hatchback, but also as a sedan), which was the American market version of the Nissan Tiida. It belonged to the first generation (C11) and was focused on providing maximum interior space and comfort within the small car segment. The 1.8 SL trim was equipped with a 1.8-liter four-cylinder engine producing around 122–126 horsepower and featured front-wheel drive. A key feature of the Versa, especially in the SL trim, was the use of a Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT), which helped boost fuel economy. The SL version was the top trim, including amenities like alloy wheels, upgraded interior materials, and cruise control, making it one of the most spacious and well-equipped vehicles in the subcompact class.

![](https://picolio.auto123.com/10photo/nissan/versahatchback5dr-18sl.jpg)

models.apiDescription:
**Lamborghini Countach**

The Lamborghini Countach was made as a reaction to the Lamborghini 
Jarama, which engineer Paolo Stanzani considered a mistake because it was too wise for Lamborghini. Paolo Stanzani then asked Marcello Gandini to design the most extravagant car possible1.

The Lamborghini Countach is, along with the Ferrari 512 Berlinetta Boxer, the most important model on the sports car market of the 1970s.

At the Geneva International Motor Show in March 1971, Lamborghini presented a concept study named "LP500". A mass production of the vehicle was not sensitive, but the study is popular, so much so that Lamborghini decides to produce and market a model resembling it. However, many details are changed. The 5-liter V12 engine of the LP500 prototype became in 1974, with the LP400, a 4-liter that was not to become famous. The name “LP” stands for “Longitudinale Posteriore” in reference to the position of the engine

models.apiDescription:
The Koenigsegg One:1 was presented at the 2014 Geneva Motor Show held in March. Koenigsegg built six cars apart from the car presented at the Geneva Motor Show. All of which were already sold. Koenigsegg took two cars to the 2014 Goodwood Festival of Speed, where they were displayed alongside other sports cars such as the McLaren P1, the Ferrari LaFerrari, the Porsche 918 Spyder and the Pagani Huayra.

The name One:1 comes from the power-to-weight ratio (1,360 PS to 1360 kg) giving the car 1 PS per 1 kg mass. The 1,360 PS power output is the equivalent of one megawatt, which Koenigsegg claims makes the One:1 the 'world's first megacar'. The car is track focused as opposed to the previous cars made by Koenigsegg. Koenigsegg had to sacrifice a few things to be able to achieve their goal with the car. There is an airscoop on the removable roof and an extra set of radiators in the front compartment, due to this reason it is not possible to store the roof in the boot like previous models.

Credits:
